_README: THE VOCABULARY OF A PLAYER-FACING STEP NOTE. One list, two readers.
`steps[].note` is drawn on screen by the questmarks-ui detail pane, which
reads build/authored/ off disk at runtime. The quest-level `notes` field is
NOT drawn -- notes.lua's anchored pattern deliberately cannot match it -- so
the two-audience split already exists in the architecture and this file is
only ever about the per-step one.
WHY A FILE RATHER THAN TWO CODE COPIES. tools/pipeline/check_voice.py reads
this to fail the build, and questmarks-ui/notes.lua reads it to redact at
display time. Those two disagreeing is exactly the drift this project keeps
getting bitten by, so there is one list and both read it. The UI resolves it
from the questmarks install path it already knows and falls back to a
bundled copy if the file is absent, so there is no hard dependency in either
WHAT DECIDES WHETHER A WORD BELONGS IN `banned`: could a player who has
never opened this repository act on the sentence? They are told by the
README and NOTICE that the data comes from BG Wiki, so wiki vocabulary is
fine and stays -- `allowed` records that decision so nobody 'tidies' it away
later. What they cannot know is anything about how this pipeline works.
_format: translate: applied FIRST, and case-preserving. An internal noun that has a
real player-facing equivalent is substituted rather than costing its whole
sentence. `from` is matched on a word boundary.
banned: applied SECOND, to what survives translation. Any SENTENCE still
containing one of these is dropped whole; a note with nothing left becomes
empty, and an empty note makes its step non-expandable, which is correct.
`re` is a Python regex; the Lua side derives an equivalent pattern.
allowed: not enforced -- documentation of what must NOT be added to banned.

translate.why: the ladder metaphor is the authoring tool's; the panel says 'step'
internal structure name; the player sees a list of steps
panel.lua already tells the player 'The game gives no signal between steps N and M'

banned.say: a Windower resource table; no player has read one
a numbered rule has no referent for a player

name resolution is invisible to the player. NO leading  : 'unresolvable' and 'unresolved' are the same build word with a prefix, and the boundary made the gate miss them while questmarks-ui's plain substring caught them -- the two sides disagreeing on 7 sentences, which is what this one file exists to prevent
any schema field name -- source_bullets, items_alt, items_partial, review_flags, by_npc, dat_names, start_disagrees_with_header
the other addon; a build input
the per-step confidence tier is a build concept

'this step carries none' is describing the record, not the game. The OBJECT is restricted on purpose: a bare 'carry no ...' also matches 'you carry no crystals', which is a genuine player instruction, so only our own nouns count
'the record' is the authored JSON, not anything the player has

banned.re: un-?modell\w*| cannot be expressed | the schema cannot
banned.say: a limitation of our data model, not of the game. Matches 'unmodellable' as well as 'unmodelled' -- same reason as resolver above
a hand pin is a build-time correction
'the step is kept anyway' is about our record, not about the game

_not_banned_deliberately: 'the addon cannot see X' -- 110 sentences, and every one is HONEST
TRANSPARENCY in plain English about a real limitation: 'the addon cannot
see party size, so the step asks for one', 'game time is invisible to the
addon'. That tells a player why no marker appears, which is the same
register panel.lua already uses -- 'The game gives no signal between steps
N and M'. It contains no jargon and a player can act on it. Banning it was
tried and reverted; it is not a leak, it is the feature.
'a ??? can never carry a marker' -- same argument. A player who can see
there is no marker on this step benefits from being told why. What is
banned is the half-sentence that follows it in the corpus -- 'but it keeps
the rung' -- which is bookkeeping about the record, and that is what

_dead._why: REMOVED after measuring: 59 hits, 59 false positives. 'Flag' is ordinary FFXI player vocabulary -- 'speaking to him is what flags the mission', 'only members with the op flagged can enter', 'flags To Paste a Peiste'. That is exactly the sentence a player wants. The internal senses are `review_flags` and 'flagged grid_conflict', and BOTH already match snake_case_field, so this rule caught nothing the list did not already have and cost 59 good sentences. Kept as a tombstone so it is not re-added.

allowed: and every in-game name -- quests, NPCs, items, zones, monsters
